summary: 1966 R-6 tower in the Lolo National Forest replacing a 1934 pole lookout, restaffed in 1995, now a Forest Service rental.

facts.design: R-6 flat cab, 41-foot treated timber tower

staffing.status: unstaffed; last known staffing continuous through at least 1968, restaffed briefly starting 1995

access.note: Forest Service rental cabin; locked gate and cabin, access code sent with reservation

visit.trail_note: set on a rock pinnacle; max stay 3 nights per reservation

facts.agency: U.S. Forest Service - Lolo National Forest

events.note: original 20-foot pole tower with L-4 cab
current 41-foot R-6 flat-cab treated timber tower built
Mike Erickson recorded as lookout staff 1966-1968, the last name in the known personnel roster before the gap
lookout staffed again, the first time in several years per NHLR
registered on the National Historic Lookout Register, August 28, 2012

evidence.supports: 1934 pole tower predecessor, 1966 current tower, restaffed in 1995
evidence.quote: This 41' treated timber tower with R-6 flat cab, built in 1966 on a beautiful rock pinnacle in the Bitterroot Mountains of western Montana at an elevation of 5900', was preceded by a 20' pole tower and L-4 cab built in 1934, which was used as a lookout until at least 1965. The present lookout was finally staffed again in 1995 for the first time in several years.

evidence.supports: NHLR registry number US 947 and registration date August 28, 2012
evidence.quote:
Up Up Lookout
US 947, MT 58 ... Date Registered

Known lookout personnel: 1955: Robert Minor; 1956: Joe McBride; 1959: Paul Eve; 1961: Robert Ferguson; 1962: William Hollenberg; 1965: Kenneth Asleson; 1966-1968: Mike Erickson.

evidence.supports: rental facility details, shift to aircraft fire detection, rec.gov's differing build-decade claim, 3-night stay limit, locked gate/cabin
evidence.quote: The wooden tower was built in the 1930s and used as a fire lookout for several years... With the growing use of aircraft for fire detection, fewer lookouts have been staffed in recent years and many are converted to cabin rentals. THE LOOKOUT CAN SLEEP UP TO FOUR PEOPLE AND IS EQUIPPED WITH ONE TWIN BED AND MATTRESS PAD. IT IS RECOMMENED TO BRING ADDITIONAL COTS TO SLEEP ON. It has propane lights and a heater. There are no cooking facilities or refrigeration. A campfire ring with a grill and a picnic table are provided at the base of the tower, along with an outhouse with a pit toilet. The entry gate and cabin remain locked; a key code will be sent to you in your reservation confirmation. Maximum stay limit is 3 nights per reservation.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: recreation.gov's listing says the wooden tower was 'built in the 1930s,' which conflicts with NHLR and firelookout.com both giving 1966 for the current tower; likely the rec.gov copy is describing the 1934 predecessor tower rather than the structure now standing, but this is not confirmed

notes_for_editor: Flagged the 1930s vs 1966 build-year discrepancy between recreation.gov and NHLR/firelookout.com in both the story and resolved_conflicts; did not find a source that explicitly reconciles it.
